# Capstone Part 1: Data Acquisition and EDA

## Overview
The capstone is where everything comes together into one portfolio-worthy project, and Part 1 focuses on the foundation that determines whether the whole project succeeds: understanding and preparing your data. You start by acquiring your chosen dataset, whether from a source like Kaggle, a public API, or your own web scraping, and loading it reliably. Then you conduct a comprehensive EDA: examine every variable's distribution, understand relationships and correlations, identify missing values, outliers, and data quality issues, and, crucially, write down the insights and hypotheses you discover, because this analysis will guide your modeling choices. Next you clean and prepare the data: handle missing values thoughtfully, fix inconsistencies, and engineer initial features. Throughout, you document your data understanding clearly, this is what turns a notebook into a professional deliverable a reader can follow. Real practitioners spend the majority of their time on exactly this phase, because a model built on poorly understood, messy data will fail no matter how sophisticated the algorithm. By the end of Part 1 you should deeply understand your data and have a clean dataset ready for modeling.

## Deep Dive
This module covers: Sourcing and loading your dataset; Comprehensive exploratory data analysis; Data cleaning and preparation; Documenting data understanding; Formulating hypotheses to test. Mastering these ideas is essential because they appear repeatedly in production AI systems.

### What You Will Learn
- The core theory behind today's topic.
- How to apply it using Python, NumPy, Pandas, or the relevant framework.
- How to evaluate results and avoid common mistakes.
- Where to find authoritative references when you need deeper detail.

### Real-World Context
In industry, these skills are used daily: data scientists clean messy survey data, AI engineers deploy models to REST APIs, and automation engineers orchestrate pipelines. Today's practical task simulates one of these real-world scenarios.

## Hands-On Practice
Practical Task: Load your capstone dataset, run a full EDA with visualizations and summary statistics, document at least five key insights, and produce a cleaned, prepared version of the data.
Mini Project: Complete and commit Part 1 of your capstone: a well-documented notebook covering data acquisition, thorough EDA, data cleaning, initial feature engineering, and a written summary of findings and hypotheses.
Assignment: Write a 'data understanding' section for your capstone that describes the dataset, its quality issues, and the top insights from your EDA.

Complete all three sections. Each completed section earns points toward your CalibiAI Score. If you are unsure about any part, use the AI assessment popup to submit your work and receive dynamic feedback from DeepSeek.

## Common Mistakes to Avoid
Many beginners rush into coding before fully understanding the data. Others skip validation steps and overestimate model performance. This module helps you build the discipline of checking assumptions first, then applying algorithms systematically.

## Career Impact
The skills covered today are frequently tested in technical interviews and required in entry-level AI engineering roles. Building a portfolio that demonstrates mastery of these concepts will significantly improve your job prospects.

## Key Takeaways
1. Theory guides practice — understand before coding.
2. Clean data and clear metrics are more valuable than complex models.
3. Document your steps for reproducibility.
4. Communication matters: explain results to non-technical stakeholders.

## Next Steps After Today
- Complete the practical task and submit it for AI review.
- Read any research papers linked for deeper theory.
- Prepare questions for tomorrow's module.

## Resources
- Use the linked videos and documentation as reference material.
- Read the research papers for theoretical depth.
- Check the GitHub repositories for working code examples.

## Assessment
After finishing the work, open the AI Assessment popup to submit your practical results. DeepSeek will evaluate your submission, calculate a dynamic score based on correctness and depth, and add the points to your CalibiAI profile.
